title: "ACLs and Edge NAT"
---

# ACLs and Edge NAT

Two small labs. The first is an ACL on the cEOS switch that already routes between VLANs. The second is source NAT on a Linux node in front of one server. They teach different tools. Do not run them as one topology.

## Learning goals

By the end of this chapter you can:

- Write an extended ACL that denies one host and permits the rest
- Apply it inbound on an SVI and prove the direction
- Masquerade a LAN behind one address on a Linux gateway
- Undo both without locking yourself out of management

## Lab A — ACL

Reuse Inter-VLAN Routing. h1 is 172.16.10.11. h2 is 172.16.20.11. Add:

```text
ip access-list BLOCK-H1
   10 deny ip host 172.16.10.11 host 172.16.20.11
   20 permit ip any any
interface Vlan10
   ip access-group BLOCK-H1 in
```

Management0 is not in VLAN 10. The ACL cannot cut your CLI session. That is deliberate. An ACL on the management interface is how people lock a lab.

```bash
docker exec clab-svi-h1 ping -c 2 172.16.20.11
docker exec clab-svi-sw Cli -c "show ip access-lists BLOCK-H1"
```

The ping fails and the deny counter moves. A second host in VLAN 10, if you add one at .12, still reaches h2 because the permit matches.

### Drill

Move the ACL to Vlan10 `out`. The counter stops moving and the ping works, because traffic from h1 arrives inbound on Vlan10. Put it back to `in`.

## Lab B — NAT

```yaml
name: nat
topology:
  nodes:
    gw:
      kind: linux
      image: alpine:latest
      exec:
        - apk add --no-cache iptables
        - sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
        - ip addr add 172.16.10.1/24 dev eth1
        - ip link set eth1 up
        - ip addr add 203.0.113.1/24 dev eth2
        - ip link set eth2 up
        - iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth2 -j MASQUERADE
    inside:
      kind: linux
      image: alpine:latest
      exec:
        - ip addr add 172.16.10.10/24 dev eth1
        - ip link set eth1 up
        - ip route add default via 172.16.10.1
    outside:
      kind: linux
      image: alpine:latest
      exec:
        - ip addr add 203.0.113.10/24 dev eth1
        - ip link set eth1 up
  links:
    - endpoints: ["inside:eth1", "gw:eth1"]
    - endpoints: ["gw:eth2", "outside:eth1"]
```

`apk` needs a path to the internet from the management interface while the container starts. If `apk` fails, the image has no iptables and the lab stops there. Do not invent a second NAT tool.

```bash
docker exec clab-nat-inside ping -c 2 203.0.113.10
docker exec clab-nat-gw iptables -t nat -L POSTROUTING -v
```

### Predict

- The ping works.
- On `outside`, a `tcpdump -ni eth1 icmp` shows the echo request from 203.0.113.1, not from 172.16.10.10.
- Delete the MASQUERADE rule. The ping fails because `outside` has no route back to 172.16.10.0/24. Add the rule again.
